A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SIM study, linear-network analysis, and diffusion-model validation despite the revised title. All 32 pages of each version, including Appendices A–G, equations, and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SIM training experiments and conditional diffusion-model results in Sections 3–5, with additional empirical results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds empirical checks of training-distribution truncation and training-set dynamics in Appendices F.3–F.4.

M1.justification: The SIM formulation, identity-mapping objective, linear and ReLU models, symmetric two-layer model, and conditional diffusion architecture are retained. Renaming Transient Memorization to Swing-by Dynamics does not change a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions study Gaussian-mixture SIM, hierarchical combinations of concepts, and synthetic circle generation varying color and size. The added sampling control and training-set diagnostics remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: The same linear and ReLU model variants are examined, and no competing method is added or removed from an evaluated comparison. The additional citations do not introduce experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix F.3 adds a controlled SIM experiment that rejects training points within half the smallest μ_p of the test point and resamples until the desired training-set size is reached. This changes sampling for the new control; the retained experiments' stated budgets and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices F.3–F.4 check training/test separation, sensitivity to truncating the training distribution, and training-loss and training-cluster trajectories alongside test dynamics. These are focused robustness and diagnostic additions to the existing analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging diffusion outputs over 32 generated images and five model seeds in Appendix G.3, and disclose tuning initialization seeds for the multiple-descent examples in E.1. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: New Figures 15–18 report little trajectory change after training-distribution truncation, monotonically decreasing training loss alongside non-monotonic test loss, and irregular training-cluster trajectories at different stages. The previously reported result curves and principal findings are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix C.2 changes the summation bounds in C.20 from d to n and in C.21 from s to n. Since n remains defined as samples per cluster, this introduces an apparent indexing inconsistency rather than an explained equivalent notation change. Theorem 4.1 and the two-layer assumptions and lemmas are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims: SIM captures compositional-learning phenomena, the analysis explains non-monotonic dynamics, and diffusion experiments validate the predictions. Swing-by Dynamics names the previously claimed Transient Memorization phenomenon.

C2.justification: Section 4.2.2 adds an applicability qualification concerning separation from training clusters. Section 3.3 now permits interpreting Swing-by as a special case of epoch-wise double descent, while Section 3.2 removes the earlier data-determined training-window interpretation of terminal slowing.

D1.justification: v2 specifies μ and σ in the Figure 2(c) caption, explicitly lists diffusion training/test compositions in Section 5, and documents rejection sampling for the new truncation control. These are added disclosures and control details, not evidence of changed retained experiments. The earlier Cannon-cluster computing acknowledgement is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations concerning invariant risk minimization, initialization, semantic learning dynamics, and double descent, including Saxe et al. (2019) and Schaeffer et al. (2023). It qualifies the relationship to double descent while retaining the broader positioning around compositional generalization and coupled linear-network dynamics.

P1.justification: The title and recurring terminology change to Swing-by Dynamics, Sections 3.2 and 5 receive localized rewrites, and F.3–F.4 are added. The author-contributions section is removed and acknowledgements change, but the overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 15–18 and redraws Figure 6 with revised labels, legends, and panel presentation. Existing figures are repositioned through layout changes; v1's data-generation Figure 15 is retained as Figure 19. Most existing plots are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix F.3 provides a targeted separation control, and F.4 adds training-set diagnostics for the Figure 5 experiment, modestly strengthening support for the OOD interpretation. Clearer diffusion descriptions and Figure 6 also help. These gains outweigh the localized loss of mathematical clarity from the unexplained summation-bound changes in C.20–C.21; the central theory and existing empirical evidence are retained.
